title: The dispute adjudicator is deliberately isolated from the parties and sees only Core GovOps' packet
content:
A.2.8.1.1.1.2 defines the split: "The Core Facilitator decides how the dispute is ultimately resolved. The Core Facilitator is isolated from the parties to maintain impartiality. The Core Facilitator exclusively reviews the information prepared by Core GovOps and delivers a decision to Core GovOps, which communicates it to the parties." A.2.8.1.1.1.1 gives Core GovOps everything else — running the process, communicating with parties, gathering and analysing information.

Isolation targets a specific risk in a small ecosystem: the adjudicator and the disputants know each other, work together continuously, and will again next month. Removing direct contact removes the channel through which relationships, lobbying and side information would otherwise reach the decision.

The price is that impartiality is purchased by making the decision-maker dependent on an intermediary. A.2.8.1.1.2.3.1 shows how much power that intermediary holds: Core GovOps' confidential analysis must include the facts, "clear identification of any areas of factual ambiguity or disagreement," a structured presentation of each side's arguments, "and a recommendation if Core GovOps believes one conclusion is clearly supported by the facts." Whoever frames the ambiguity and drafts the recommendation shapes the outcome.

Two counterweights keep this from being a rubber stamp. A.2.8.1.1.2.3.2 has the Facilitator review "the analysis prepared by Core GovOps **along with the arguments presented by the parties**," so the raw submissions travel with the summary. And the Facilitator "is free to adopt arguments presented by the parties, by Core GovOps, or to advance their own analysis," with a written decision setting out reasoning — which makes departure from the recommendation both permitted and visible.
description: The Core Facilitator decides but never engages the parties, reviewing exclusively the confidential analysis Core GovOps prepares — impartiality bought at the cost of concentrating framing power.
